en.name: Berbere
en.summary: Berbere keeps 6 months in an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard. That is the standard figure for a ground spice, and it is a flavour window rather than a safety limit — old berbere is dull and faded, not dangerous.
en.pantry: 6 months in an airtight jar, cool, dark cupboard, dry hands and a dry spoon. Berbere is a ground blend and follows the usual 6-month rule for ground spices, but two things shorten it further. The chilli pigment bleaches in daylight, so a jar on a sunny shelf goes orange and dull within weeks. And the blend is often slightly damp from the fenugreek and the ginger in it, so it cakes. Damp berbere in a warm kitchen can genuinely mould — break up any hard lumps and look at them before you use them.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for berbere. The cupboard is where a ground blend belongs, and the fridge adds humidity to a spice that is already prone to caking. If you live somewhere hot and humid and want to keep the colour, use a properly airtight jar and let it come fully to room temperature before you open it, so condensation does not land on the powder.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published either. Cold would slow the pigment and the aroma fading, but the condensation problem is worse than in the fridge and berbere cakes readily to begin with. Buying small and using it within the window is more effective than any cold storage trick. Wet berbere paste — delek berbere or awaze, made up with water, wine or oil — is a fresh condiment and belongs in the refrigerator instead.
en.thawing: Not applicable. Berbere is a dry cupboard spice; the wet paste made from it is a refrigerated condiment.
spoilage: A dull orange-brown colour where the blend was deep red.
Little or no smell when you warm a pinch in your palm.
Hard lumps, which mean moisture has got into the jar.
Any visible mould inside a lump, which means the jar goes.
tips: Use an opaque jar or keep it in a dark cupboard; daylight bleaches chilli fast.
Only ever use a dry spoon, and never shake it over a steaming pot.
Buy small quantities and make it up fresh if you can.
Bloom it in hot oil or niter kibbeh at the start of a dish to wake the aroma up.

faq.a: 6 months in an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard.
No, just faded. Ground spices lose aroma and colour rather than becoming unsafe. Mould in a caked, damp jar is the exception.

faq.q: Why has my berbere gone orange?
faq.a: Light has bleached the chilli pigment. Keep it in an opaque container or a dark cupboard, away from the window and the hob.

zh.name: 衣索比亞綜合辣香料（berbere）
zh.summary: berbere 裝在氣密罐、放陰涼避光的櫥櫃可放 6 個月。這是研磨香料的標準數字，而且是風味的窗口而不是安全的上限——放久的 berbere 是顏色和香氣都退掉，不是變危險。
zh.pantry: 氣密罐、陰涼避光的櫥櫃，手要乾、湯匙也要乾，6 個月。berbere 是研磨的綜合香料，適用研磨香料通用的六個月規則；但有兩件事會讓它更短。辣椒色素在日光下會漂白，所以一罐放在有陽光層架上的 berbere，幾週內就會變成暗橘色、顏色死掉。再者，配方裡的葫蘆巴和薑常讓粉略帶濕氣，所以它容易結塊。在溫暖廚房裡受潮的 berbere 是真的可能發霉——把硬塊撥開，看清楚了再用。
zh.fridge: berbere 沒有公布的冷藏期限。研磨綜合香料該待的地方是櫥櫃，而冰箱只會替一個本來就容易結塊的香料再加上濕氣。如果你住在又熱又濕的地方、又想保住顏色，請用真正氣密的罐子，並且讓它完全回到室溫再打開，免得結露落在粉上。
zh.freezer: 冷凍同樣沒有期限數據。低溫確實能拖慢色素與香氣流失，但結露問題比冷藏更嚴重，而 berbere 本來就很會結塊。買少量、在窗口內用完，比任何低溫保存的小技巧都有效。用水、酒或油調成的濕 berbere 醬（delek berbere／awaze）則是新鮮的醬料，該放冷藏。
zh.thawing: 不適用。berbere 是乾燥的櫥櫃香料；用它調成的濕醬則是冷藏的醬料。
spoilage: 原本深紅的粉變成暗沉的橘褐色。
在手心搓熱一小撮，幾乎聞不到香氣。
出現硬塊，代表水氣跑進罐子了。
硬塊裡看得到霉——那整罐就該丟。
tips: 用不透光的罐子，或收在暗處；日光漂白辣椒的速度很快。
永遠用乾湯匙，也不要在冒蒸氣的鍋子上方抖罐子。
少量購買，可以的話自己現調。
下鍋時先用熱油或澄清香料奶油炒香，把香氣叫醒。

faq.a: 氣密罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，6 個月。

faq.q: 放久的 berbere 有危險嗎？
faq.a: 沒有，只是退了。研磨香料是失去香氣與顏色，而不是變得不安全。受潮結塊長霉是唯一的例外。

faq.q: 我的 berbere 為什麼變橘色了？
faq.a: 光線把辣椒色素漂白了。請改用不透光容器或收進暗櫃，遠離窗邊和爐台。
